knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/problem:
Simplify to a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
\frac{\frac{1}{2}\sin\left(13^\circ\right)\cos\left(13^\circ\right)}{\cos\left(26^\circ\right)}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=13^\circ$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\frac{1}{2}\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=\frac{1}{4}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{1}{4}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{1}{4}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=13^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=26^\circ$. The result is

$$
\frac{1}{4}\tan\left(26^\circ\right) .
$$

knowledge_point.title: Using the Double-Angle Formula to Simplify Products

question.:question/problem:
Simplify the expression, using the sine of twice the given angle.

$$
\left(\sin\left(41^\circ\right)-\cos\left(41^\circ\right)\right)^2
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=41^\circ$. Expand the square and combine the squared terms.

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\sin x-\cos x)^2 &=\sin^2 x-2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2 x \\ &=1-2\sin x\cos x \\ &=1-\sin(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $\sin^2 x+\cos^2 x=1$ and $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$. The cross-term sign is negative.

Substitute $x=41^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=82^\circ$. The result is

$$
1-\sin\left(82^\circ\right) .
$$

question.:question/problem:
Simplify to a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
\frac{3\cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{7}\right)\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{7}\right)}{\cos\left(\frac{6\pi}{7}\right)}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=\frac{3\pi}{7}$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{3\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=\frac{3}{2}\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=\frac{3}{2}\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=\frac{3\pi}{7}$ and double the whole angle: $2x=\frac{6\pi}{7}$. The result is

$$
\frac{3}{2}\tan\left(\frac{6\pi}{7}\right) .
$$

question.:question/problem:
Simplify to a constant multiple of a single trigonometric ratio.

$$
\frac{-4\cos\left(31^\circ\right)\sin\left(31^\circ\right)}{\cos\left(62^\circ\right)}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Put $x=31^\circ$. Recall $2\sin x\cos x=\sin(2x)$.

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{-4\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} &=-2\frac{2\sin x\cos x}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-2\frac{\sin(2x)}{\cos(2x)} \\ &=-2\tan(2x)
\end{aligned}
$$

The denominator is nonzero, and $\tan(2x)=\sin(2x)/\cos(2x)$.

Substitute $x=31^\circ$ and double the whole angle: $2x=62^\circ$. The result is

$$
-2\tan\left(62^\circ\right) .
$$
